solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leader of Michigan's on different Great Lake as abbess

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of the state name Michigan

parts.note: different means other
Lake Superior is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A Michigan politician takes office on another Great Lake as head of a nunnery.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent of nuns is addressed by this title, the female counterpart of an abbot.

clue.text: Very enthusiastic deliveries by injured Broad

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, i.e. deliveries

indicators.note: injured suggests the name is damaged and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the bowler Stuart Broad, carrying an injury, sends down some wild balls.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuart Broad is an English fast bowler, which makes 'deliveries' look like bowling; 'injured' turns BROAD into BOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Going overboard is an idiom for being excessively keen or enthusiastic about something.

clue.text: This is why female goes to church

parts.note: a hen is a female bird, and by extension a female
CE is short for Church of England

explanation.surface: Explaining a woman's churchgoing habit.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb introduces a consequence, equivalent to 'for this reason' or 'therefore'.

clue.text: Poor scores in Liverpool strip, passed over again

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the kit colour

parts.note: Liverpool FC play in a red kit (strip is British for a team's kit)

indicators.note: poor suggests the scores are bad, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Bad results for Liverpool's team as the ball is passed back again.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool Football Club play in red; 'Poor' rearranges the scores into CROSSE, and 'in' puts that inside the kit colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To recross is to cross back over, so the past tense describes going over something a second time.

clue.text: Join endless retinue heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means reading upwards, i.e. backwards
endless says to drop both end letters of the printed word retinue

explanation.surface: Joining a royal entourage as it travels north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips RETINUE to ETINU, and 'heading north' reads that upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To join things together is to bring them into union, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Religious probes dubious miracle as observer

indicators.note: probes means goes into, so one piece is placed inside the other
dubious suggests the word is doubtful and to be rearranged

parts.note: PI is short for pious, i.e. religious

explanation.surface: A devout person investigates a questionable miracle as an onlooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as observer' is an unusual definition: empirical knowledge comes from observing. 'dubious' gives EMRICAL and 'probes' puts the pious abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge gained as an observer, through experience and observation rather than theory, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Writer Dorothy entertains one nincompoop

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as I

indicators.note: entertains means holds within, so one letter goes inside the name

parts.note: Dot is a short form of Dorothy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A novelist named Dorothy hosts a single guest who turns out to be a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a foolish person, a plain synonym of a dimwit.

clue.text: Soldiers don't finish course of therapy

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a regiment is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops abandon their medical treatment partway through.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed plan of diet, exercise or medication is a regimen, a course of treatment.

clue.text: Mislay disc cases successfully completed

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the disc abbreviation wraps the other piece

parts.note: CD is a compact disc
to mislay is to lose

explanation.surface: Losing the boxes your CDs came in.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal that has been closed has been concluded or finalised successfully.

clue.text: Right to take one long sleep

indicators.note: to take means to hold within, so the numeral is placed inside

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Claiming one's entitlement to sleep late.
explanation.walkthrough: A LIEN is a legal right over someone's property; I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is staying in bed later than usual in the morning, a long sleep.

clue.text: It's severely harming credit piling up round Portugal

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the anagram wraps the country code
up as in disturbed or in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: Mounting credit debts in Portugal are causing serious damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges the piling into IPLING, and 'round' wraps it around Portugal's code; 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crippling damages so badly that it disables, as in crippling debts.

clue.text: Extremely nippy wild zebus run out

indicators.note: wild suggests the animals run riot, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: Wild zebus, a kind of cattle, have fled in freezing weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Below freezing point is extremely cold, and nippy means chilly.

clue.text: Misprint — rare mistake by corporation

indicators.note: a mistake garbles the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a paunch, so a tum or belly

explanation.surface: A rare typing error by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' as a pot belly is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printing or writing, often listed on a correction slip.

clue.text: Doctor's at home grabbing a catheter

indicators.note: grabbing means holding inside, so the article goes into the pair of pieces

parts.note: DR is short for doctor
in means at home

explanation.surface: A doctor at home seizes a medical tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A catheter is a tube for draining fluid from the body, and a drain is such a tube in surgery.

clue.text: Poverty seen to be rising, eats in

indicators.note: in places the eating word inside the turned-round word
in a down clue rising means read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: dines means eats

explanation.surface: Being seen to rise and eat at home is a mark of being poor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'to be rising' reads upwards, giving NEES; 'in' takes the eating word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neediness is the state of being in want, so a synonym for poverty.

clue.text: Mark's monocle is smashed

indicators.note: a smashed eyeglass is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's eyeglass has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark's' looks like a man's name; it is the definition, with ''s' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicolon is a punctuation mark, so mark is its broader category.

clue.text: After a short month, adult working with editor changed tune

indicators.note: after says the next pieces follow the abbreviated month

parts.note: mo is an abbreviation for month

indicators.note: working suggests the word is worked over, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shortly into the month a grown-up working with an editor changed their tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To modulate in music is to change key, so a tune that modulated changed its key.

clue.text: Profitable victualler, not large, goes bust

indicators.note: going bust breaks something up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not means without, so one letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A pub landlord, not a big operator, goes bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: A victualler supplies food and drink; a licensed victualler runs a British pub. 'not' drops one L to leave VICTUALER, which 'goes bust' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative means producing a good deal of money, so profitable.

clue.text: He dreaded playing matches like this

indicators.note: playing as in playing about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man feared playing with matches.
explanation.walkthrough: Matches with red tips are described by the answer, so 'matches like this' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary safety matches have red heads of chemical compound on the end of each stick.

clue.text: Kane's last word: scatty subeditor missed it

indicators.note: scatty means scatterbrained, so the letters are rearranged
missed says two letters are removed from the fodder before rearranging

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained subeditor overlooked something in the copy.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Foster Kane's dying word in the film Citizen Kane names his childhood sledge. SUBEDITOR without I and T leaves letters that 'scatty' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: In Citizen Kane the tycoon dies uttering this single word, the mystery the film investigates.

clue.text: Apart from house, alcohol's drunk here

definitions.text: Apart from house, alcohol's drunk here

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated, so the letters are rearranged
apart from means without, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A pub is where, rather than at home, one drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing HO from ALCOHOL leaves ALCOL, which 'drunk' rearranges; the whole clue also describes a British local, one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a local is the pub nearest your home, where you go to drink.

clue.text: First violinist announced songs

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the word said aloud gives the answer

parts.note: the principal first violinist of an orchestra is called its leader

explanation.surface: The orchestra's principal violinist has announced the programme of songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, such as those by Schubert for voice and piano.

clue.text: EU farm scheme has no time for holiday location

indicators.note: has no means lacks, so one letter is removed

parts.note: set-aside was the EU scheme paying farmers to leave land fallow

explanation.surface: A European agriculture policy leaves no time for a break away.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast is a classic holiday destination, a resort by the sea.

clue.text: One chased by mad Cortez, stripping gold

definitions.text: One chased by mad Cortez, stripping gold

indicators.note: chased by means followed by, so the remaining letters come after

parts.note: A means one

indicators.note: mad suggests crazed, so the letters are rearranged
stripping means taking away, so letters are removed

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: The conquistador Cortés pursued Mexican natives and stripped them of their gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing OR from CORTEZ leaves CTEZ, which 'mad' rearranges into ZTEC; the clue as a whole describes the Spanish conquest of Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés conquered this Mexican empire and looted its gold.

clue.text: Delicate, slight and somewhat self-interested

indicators.note: somewhat means partly, so the answer is a part of the word

explanation.surface: A description of a frail, rather selfish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicately built, like an elf.

clue.text: It escapes in period after lake gets polluted

indicators.note: after says the period word follows the rearranged letters
polluting spoils the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something seeps out of a lake that has been fouled over a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is what escapes through a leak, as with fluid or information.

clue.text: It distends atria, collecting oxygen for one

indicators.note: distends means swells out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
collecting oxygen means taking in the element symbol in place of another letter
for means in place of, so the oxygen symbol replaces the numeral one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A heart chamber swelling as it gathers oxygenated blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' and 'for' swap O in for I, turning ATRIA into ATROA, which 'distends' rearranges. 'It' is the definition: the main artery is one thing that stretches as blood is pumped in.
explanation.definitionFit: The bare pronoun stands for the body's main artery, the subject of the clue's surface.

clue.text: Target of ridicule after faulty dairy product

parts.note: a butt is the target of jokes or mockery

indicators.note: faulty means defective, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is mocked after a defective food product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a charade signal, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfat is the fat content of milk, from which butter is made.

clue.text: Haul up beams by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is said aloud, signalling a homophone

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Lifting the girders in a building job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' suggests timber hauled up; it is RAYS of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift or hoist it up.

clue.text: Dodge bunker tools (about 500) in 22 game

parts.note: to duck is to dodge

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the Roman numeral sits within

parts.note: sand rakes are used to smooth golf course bunkers
D is the Roman numeral 500

explanation.surface: Avoiding the rakes left in a golf bunker during a seaside game.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 refers to the answer at 22-across, a seaside setting; the game is skimming flat stones across water.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastime of skipping stones across the sea's surface is played at the shore.
